question: Does independent spatial mapping of Torgersen sub-colony attrition converge with the census-derived colony-network erosion signal, without claiming an unresolved colony-code-to-polygon crosswalk?

tests.T1_spatial_contraction: External mapping must show substantial contraction in the number of historically occupied sub-colony footprints.
tests.T2_nonrandom_topographic_attrition: External mapping must show that extinction/persistence is structured by independent physical habitat attributes such as aspect, elevation, or historic colony area.
tests.T3_internal_predictive_signal: The frozen mina effective-colony-number result must retain positive coefficient and positive held-out-year gain.
tests.T4_identifier_crosswalk: A formal identifier-level validation is allowed only if a machine-readable mapping from LTER colony_code to external polygon IDs is available.

decision_logic.causal_fragmentation_claim: prohibited unless identifier-level mapping plus independent topographic measurements are joined under a new prospective design

interpretation_boundaries: The 2025 spatial study overlaps the Palmer demographic system and therefore is external spatial evidence, not a wholly independent population replication.
Do not equate effective colony number with mapped habitat area or physical connectivity.
Do not infer that large colonies are intrinsically protective; the >50-pair directional validation already failed.
Do not claim colony-code-level topographic validation until the crosswalk is resolved.
This stage adds no new tuned colony topology metric.
terminal_rule: For the core paper, use this as spatial triangulation only. Further work must resolve the colony-code/polygon crosswalk or remain separate future research.
